pages.title: Linear attention
claims: Consider the usual attention operation.. 𝑄 ∈ 𝑅 𝑛×𝑑𝑘 , 𝐾 ∈ 𝑅 𝑛×𝑑𝑘 , 𝑉 ∈ 𝑅 𝑛×𝑑𝑣
This is quadratic due to 𝑄𝐾 ⊤ (𝑛 2 𝑑𝑘 ). Can we do better (when 𝜌 is the identity)?
This is very silly, but surprisingly important.. We get from 𝑛 2 𝑑𝑘 + 𝑛 2 𝑑𝑣 to 2𝑛𝑑𝑣 𝑑𝑘
figures_mentioned: [Shen et al 2018, Katharopoulos 2020 for kernel version. Also connections to things like fast weight programmers]
dropped: 𝐴𝑡𝑡𝑛 𝑄, 𝐾, 𝑉 = 𝜌 𝑄𝐾 ⊤ 𝑉

pages.title: Recurrent form of linear attention
claims: Recall that in purely linear attention, we consider the reordering
This is linear time (great) but the even nicer thing is that this looks like a RNN.
𝑆𝑡 = 𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡 𝑣𝑡⊤ and 𝑦𝑡 = 𝑞𝑡⊤ 𝑆𝑡
This ‘duality’ allows us to train efficiently (using the parallel, quadratic form) and
inference efficiently (using the serial, linear form)
(Note: if one weights 𝑆𝑡−1 by 𝛾, you get a RetNet)

pages.title: Minimax M1
claims: Minimax M1 (and minimax-text-01) use a 7-to-1 hybrid (7 linear, 1 full) linear attention.
Performance (generally) seems strong, and they show linear scaling in context length

pages.title: From linear attention to Mamba-2
claims: Let’s generalize linear attention a little bit and add per-position weights..
𝑆𝑡 = 𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡 𝑣𝑡⊤ and 𝑦𝑡 = 𝑞𝑡⊤ 𝑆𝑡 (Linear attention)
𝑆𝑡 = 𝛾𝑡 𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡 𝑣𝑡⊤ and 𝑦𝑡 = 𝑞𝑡⊤ 𝑆𝑡 + 𝑣𝑡⊤ 𝐷 with 𝛾𝑡 = 𝑓(𝑥𝑡 )(Mamba-2)
There is a lot more words to justify this (go read the mamba 2 paper) but the mechanics
is that we can make linear attention more expressive via gating (gating is good!)
This continues to have duality properties (compute 𝛾 in parallel, apply duality)

pages.title: Nemotron 3

pages.title: Gated delta net (and friends)
claims: Let’s generalize things further – gate the input and selectively erase the state.
𝑆𝑡 = 𝛾𝑡 𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡 𝑣𝑡⊤ and 𝑦𝑡 = 𝑞𝑡⊤ 𝑆𝑡 + 𝑣𝑡⊤ 𝐷 with 𝛾𝑡 = 𝑓(𝑥𝑡 )(Mamba-2)
𝑆𝑡 = 𝛾𝑡 (𝐼 − 𝛽𝑡 𝑘𝑡 𝑘𝑡⊤ )𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝛽𝑡 𝑘𝑡 𝑣𝑡⊤ and
𝑦𝑡 = 𝑞𝑡⊤ 𝑆𝑡 with 𝛾𝑡 = 𝑓 𝑥𝑡 , 𝛽𝑡 = 𝑓 𝑥𝑡 (Gated Delta Net)
The gated delta net adds a ‘no input operation’ gate (𝛽 = 0)
And erases anything in the direction of the current key (𝐼 − 𝛽𝑡 𝑘𝑡 𝑘𝑡⊤ )
Close relationships to various fast weight programming / test time training ideas.

pages.title: How do we train MoEs?
claims: Major challenge: we need sparsity for training-time efficiency…
But sparse gating decisions are not differentiable!
Solutions?
1. Reinforcment learning to optimize gating policies
2. Stochastic perturbations
3. Heuristic ‘balancing’ losses.
Guess which one people use in practice?

claims: 1. This naturally leads to experts that are a bit more robust.

The derivative with respect to 𝑝𝑖 (𝑥) is 𝑇 2 σ 1𝑎𝑟𝑔𝑚𝑎𝑥 𝑝 𝑥 =𝑖 ,
so more frequent use = stronger downweighting
cites: From the Switch Transformer [Fedus et al 2022]

pages.title: Bonus: What else do you need to make DeepSeek MoE v3?
claims: MLA : Multihead, latent attention
Basic idea: express the Q, K, V as functions of a lower-dim, ‘latent’ activation

pages.title: What else do you need to make DeepSeek MoE v3?
claims: Basic idea: express the Q, K, V as functions of a lower-dim, ‘latent’ activation
Benefits: when KV-caching, we only need to store 𝑐𝑡𝐾𝑉 , which can be much smaller.
𝑊 𝑈𝐾 can be merged into the Q projection
(they also compress queries, for memory savings during training)
Complexity: rope conflicts with MLA-style caching.
Without RoPE – 𝑄, 𝐾 = ℎ𝑊 𝑄 , 𝑊 𝑈𝐾 𝑐𝑡𝐾𝑉 = ⟨ℎ 𝑊 𝑄 𝑊 𝑈𝐾 , 𝑐𝑡𝐾𝑉 ⟩
With RoPE - 𝑄𝑅𝑞 , 𝑅𝑘 𝐾 = ℎ𝑊 𝑄 𝑅𝑞 , 𝑅𝑘 𝑊 𝑈𝐾 𝑐𝑡𝐾𝑉 = ℎ 𝑊 𝑄 𝑅𝑞 𝑅𝑘 𝑊 𝑈𝐾 , 𝑐𝑡𝐾𝑉
The solution – Have a few non-latent key dimensions that can be rotated
